extracted.intended_audience: IRF (inpatient rehabilitation facility) administrators, hospital finance officers, Medicare Administrative Contractors, health policy stakeholders, and commenters on CMS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final policies for calculating the FY 2025 IRF labor-related share and wage index, implementing updated OMB CBSA delineations, and transition/mitigation policies for affected rehabilitation facilities. Includes methodological specifications, data sources, caps, and phase-out rules used to determine IRF PPS payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of labor-related share
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify a cost category as labor-related if the costs are labor-intensive and vary with the local labor market; labor-related share determined by identifying the national average proportion of total costs that are related to, influenced by, or vary with the local labor market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy continues the historic approach of designating cost categories as labor-related when labor intensity and sensitivity to local labor market conditions are evident. See FY 2024 IRF PPS rule for additional methodology background.

rubrics_metrics.name: FY 2025 labor-related share calculation (2021-based IRF market basket)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the FY 2025 labor-related share as the sum of the FY 2025 relative importance of: Wages and Salaries; Employee Benefits; Professional Fees: Labor-Related; Administrative and Facilities Support Services; Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Services; All Other: Labor-Related Services; plus a portion of the Capital-Related relative importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using IGI forecasts for the 2021-based IRF market basket, CMS computed operating labor-related subtotal (70.5–70.7%) and applied 46% of Capital-Related (8.1% × 46% = 3.7%) to reach a total labor-related share (finalized at 74.4%). The relative importance reflects price changes between base year (2021) and FY 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portion of Capital-Related costs influenced by local labor market (46%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat 46 percent of Capital-Related costs as influenced by the local labor market for the purpose of determining the labor-related share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to the FY 2025 Capital relative importance (8.1%) to compute the capital-related labor share contribution (3.7 percentage points). The 46% percentage is the same used for the 2016-based IRF market basket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of most recent appropriate data for final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If more recent data become available after publication of the proposed rule and before publication of the final rule (for example, a more recent estimate of the labor-related share), CMS will use such data, if appropriate, to determine the FY 2025 values in the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS relied on IHS Global Inc.'s second quarter 2024 forecast (historical through Q1 2024) to finalize the labor-related share at 74.4% after considering public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement for wage adjustment and budget neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(j)(6) requires the Secretary to adjust the proportion of rehabilitation facilities' costs attributable to wages and wage-related costs by a factor reflecting the relative hospital wage level in the facility's geographic area compared to the national average; adjustments must be made in a budget-neutral manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wage index updates are to be based on available data concerning wages and wage-related costs for furnishing rehabilitation services and applied budget-neutrally across IRFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index data source: pre-reclassification and pre-floor IPPS wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRF PPS wage index is derived from the pre-reclassification and pre-floor inpatient PPS (IPPS) wage index data (based on hospital cost report data for cost reporting periods beginning Oct 1, 2020 through Sep 30, 2021 for FY 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS maintains that the IRF wage index is derived from IPPS wage data; changes in IPPS policies that affect wage data will be reflected in future IRF wage indices due to this derivation and the typical four-year lag in IPPS wage data.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5-percent cap on annual decreases to provider wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a permanent 5-percent cap on any decrease to a provider's wage index from its wage index in the prior year, regardless of the circumstances causing the decline; cap is applied at the provider level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New IRFs are paid the wage index for their geographic area for their first full or partial FY with no cap applied. Providers should coordinate with their MAC to determine how the 5-percent cap is implemented for their situation; MACs have been provided instructions in CMS Pub. 100-04 Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of areas with no hospital wage index data (imputation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the FY 2008 methodology to address geographic areas with no hospitals: for rural areas without hospital wage data, average wage indexes from neighboring local/contiguous counties; for urban areas without specific hospital wage data, use the average wage indexes of all urban areas within the State as a proxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in FY 2025 to impute a rural wage index for a set of rural North Dakota counties and to use state urban averages where applicable (e.g., CBSA 25980 Hinesville Fort Stewart, GA as the only urban area without hospital wage index data in FY 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of OMB CBSA delineations for wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt OMB's revised CBSA delineations (most recently OMB Bulletin No. 23-01 based on 2020 Standards) for delineating IRF labor market areas and calculating the IRF PPS wage index beginning FY 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS references prior adoptions (OMB Bulletins 13-01, 15-01, 17-01, 18-04) and describes timeline and rationale for adopting updated delineations to better reflect contemporary urban/rural areas and labor markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of counties that change urban/rural status under new CBSA delineations
rubrics_metrics.description: When CBSA delineations reclassify counties from urban to rural (or rural to urban), CMS will (a) treat hospitals in counties becoming rural as rural for wage index calculations and include hospitals in counties becoming urban in their new urban CBSAs, and (b) list and apply the changes reflected in tables of affected counties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables list 54 counties moving urban→rural and 54 moving rural→urban. Providers changing designation may experience positive or negative wage index impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year budget-neutral phase-out of rural adjustment for rural→urban transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For existing FY 2024 rural IRFs that become urban in FY 2025 and experience a loss in payments due to losing the 14.9% rural adjustment, apply a budget-neutral three-year phase-out: receive two-thirds of prior rural adjustment in FY 2025, one-third in FY 2026, and none in FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy is specifically for rural IRFs that transition to urban in FY 2025 and experience payment loss; intended to mitigate abrupt payment reductions. No additional transition besides the permanent 5% cap is applied for other changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No transition policy for urban→rural transitions (immediate rural adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: IRFs that change from urban to rural under the new delineations will receive the full rural adjustment (14.9%) beginning October 1, 2024; no phase-in transition is needed for these facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrasts with the phase-out for rural→urban transitions because urban→rural facilities gain payment via the rural adjustment immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of CBSA delineation changes budget-neutrally
rubrics_metrics.description: All CBSA delineation changes are applied budget-neutrally under the wage index — increasing some IRF wage indices while reducing others — consistent with wage index policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes that applying changed delineations budget-neutrally preserves the overall budget but reallocates payments among IRFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of using additional non-OMB data to alter OMB delineations
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS declines to modify OMB CBSA delineations using additional data for Medicare reimbursement purposes due to administrative burden, complexity, and lack of appropriateness for defining regional labor markets for IRF workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes the labor market area where the IRF is geographically located (per OMB delineations) is most appropriate and using extra data could significantly increase administrative complexity for IRFs and CMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of IPPS policy effects on IRF wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that IPPS wage index changes (for example, low wage index hospital policies) influence IRF wage indices because the IRF wage index is derived from IPPS wage data; impacts will be reflected over time due to data lags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cannot yet determine appropriateness of applying IPPS-specific adjustments directly to IRF PPS without IRF-specific wage data, though it may consider analysis of Worksheet S-3 data from Form 2552-96.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring of contract labor trends (no immediate policy change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge commenters' concerns about rising reliance on contract labor and that contract labor may not be tied to local economy; CMS will monitor trends but has not changed wage index policy in response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis of Medicare cost report data showed contract labor hours were ~4% of total compensation hours in IPPS hospitals in 2021. CMS will continue monitoring but no immediate adjustment is made for contract labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider-level application and operational guidance (MAC interaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 5-percent cap and other provider-specific applications are applied at the provider level; IRFs should consult their Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) for details on how rules apply to their circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provided instructions to MACs on applying the 5-percent cap and emphasizes that wage index tables are provided at the CBSA level while cap application is carried out at the provider level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative importance reflects price change between base year and FY
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative importance weights from the market basket reflect differing rates of price change for cost categories between the base year (2021) and FY 2025 and approximate the labor-related portion of total costs after accounting for historical and projected price changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Price proxies for different cost categories may change at different rates; the relative importance captures these changes and is used to calculate the labor-related share.
